result.topic_en: A table of complex-valued quantities P and Q at indices 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, given both in rectangular form and as logarithm of modulus with argument in degrees, minutes and seconds, followed by a list of the 'simplest canons' as complex fractions together with a stated property of their imaginary parts.

methods.what: Tabulation of complex quantities P_n, Q_n for n = 1, 2, 4, …, 64 in rectangular form and as log-modulus with argument in degrees, minutes and seconds (repeated doubling of the index)
List of the 'simplest canons' written as reduced complex fractions for successive powers of 2
Characterisation of a simplest canon by bounds on the imaginary parts of t and of 1/t
methods.quote:
Ein einfachstes Canon hat allemahl die Eigenschaft
dass der [-reel-] imaginäre Theil
von $t$ zwischen $-i$ und $+i$
von $\frac{1}{t}$ zwischen $-2i$ und $+2i$
liegt.

items.quote:
Ein einfachstes Canon hat allemahl die Eigenschaft
dass der [-reel-] imaginäre Theil
von $t$ zwischen $-i$ und $+i$
von $\frac{1}{t}$ zwischen $-2i$ und $+2i$
liegt.
items.english: A simplest canon always has the property that the imaginary part of t lies between −i and +i, and that of 1/t between −2i and +2i.
